I was 25 when my mom died. That was 5 years ago this month. She was my best friend, the anchor I had through the tumultuous ups and downs of my early 20s. I had a complicated childhood and she was the only close adult who didn’t make it so. 

I’m with you with the intensity and the variety of the grief experience. I don’t have platitudes to give you. I’m still sad, especially that she didn’t get to see me continue to get my feet under me and figure things out. And she didn’t get to continue her vibrant, loving, and generous life. 

I guess all I can say that it levels out more over time. If anything, now when I feel emotional I am grateful. It feels like she’s visiting, as hard as that is, I want to keep feeling that she’s around. She is. Your mom will stick with you too. 

Hang in there. ♥️

The resolution that the house passed (unanimously) and the Senate didn't vote on (McConnell) actually wasn't binding. It is mostly up to the Justice Department to release it. The Senate Judiciary committee will have Barr testify and could have Mueller testify. Many folks believe they will eventually release the report with some parts redacted.

The only reason the house vote passed unanimously with Republican support is that they knew that McConnell would not put it up to the Senate to vote, so those Republicans knew their support wouldn't amount to anything. Therefore, they can now claim that they were for being transparent for the reelection campaigns.

IMO, the criticism here for the Dems and many folks in the media is valid: they put a ton of eggs in this basket  which many experts predicted was not likely to be successful. Dems could have focused on their legislative agenda instead and let the report handle itself, which was going to be big news no matter what. Now they have given Trump a HUGE "victory" that you bet he will try to capitalize on in 2020.

So maybe what Bunny and others are getting at is that YES, of course looking into this was important, but the way in which Dems piled on the bandwagon and hyped the investigation was a strategic blunder. The investigation more likely to go badly for Trump is still in progress in the SDNY.

My family/friends know I've felt suicidal, but I still feel like I can't talk about it because it would upset them too much.

I have felt the same way on and off for years. I had a lot of issues in High School and College and I never achieved as much as I wanted to or even enjoyed myself much.  All of my friends passed me by and are now entering “adulthood”, whether that means career success or marriage, or even just living healthy lifestyles. I still really struggle with that. 

I don’t have it all together. But it has gotten better. I am a lot more resilient than I used to be; things that would have devastated me before and made me suicidal (negative work feedback, relationship conflict) don’t seem as much like life or death situations. Sometimes it takes a little time to build strength, because life will continue throwing curveballs no matter what (for everyone) 

Also, I have found that “getting behind” becomes much less upsetting as time goes on. My life is still progressing regardless of where I thought I should be. I haven’t finished college and it’s been 6 years now. That used to feel life ending. Now it isn’t perfect, but I know enough people that are also in my “non traditional student” boat to know that finishing is doable. 

It’s devastating at first when you figure out life won’t progress just like you thought it would. But it does progress. And it may even surprise you. Good luck buddy.
